governing_equation: rho_t = D_r*Delta rho - chi*div(rho*grad c) + s_rho ; c_t = D_c*Delta c + alpha*rho - beta*c + s_c
implementation_notes: 2-D Keller-Segel chemotaxis on [0,1]^2, t in [0,0.5], manufactured so the exact fields are rho = 1 + 0.2*sin(pi x)*sin(pi y)*exp(-t) (range [1, 1.2]) and c = 1 + 0.1*cos(pi x)*cos(pi y)*exp(-2t) (range [0.9, 1.1]) -- both strictly positive. Multi-field: solve_pde(N) returns fields={rho, c} on grid {x,y}, reported at t_final=0.5. Coupled reaction-diffusion with a nonlinear chemotaxis flux -chi*div(rho*grad c). Time-dependent Dirichlet BCs taken from the manufactured fields (on the boundary sin(pi x)/sin(pi y)=0 so rho=1, while c=1+0.1*cos(...)*exp(-2t)). Add the explicit manufactured sources s_rho, s_c (given in parameters, ready as NumPy expressions with X,Y meshgrid and scalar t; verified to reproduce the exact fields to FD accuracy) to the RHS. Run at N=48 and N=96; scored on relative L2 error (<1%) of BOTH rho and c on the returned grid, plus observed convergence order p=log2(err_N/err_2N)>=1.4 on the primary field rho. HARD GATE: min_density -- the chemotaxis term is the classic source of spurious negative density near aggregation; discretize the -chi*div(rho*grad c) flux with an upwind / flux-limited (positivity-preserving) scheme, NOT a bare np.maximum clip, or the solution fails as CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION regardless of accuracy. No gauge fields (both fields fully determined). Rectangular domain (no mask). Build the mesh with np.meshgrid(indexing='ij') and keep operators sparse.
